card.name: Stopping or interrupting a named drug
card.fires_on: The last piece of a drug name, or the word discontinued, when the text says to stop, interrupt or hold that drug. It appears in dosing-adjustment and warning sections.

modes.label: End of drug name after stop/interrupt
modes.description: Final piece of a brand or generic name right after a verb like stop, interrupt or discontinue.
modes.example: Interrupt JAYPIR<<CA>> until recovery to Grade 1 or baseline

modes.label: Discontinued after drug as subject
modes.description: The word discontinued or a following noun like tablets after the drug name in a should-be-stopped statement.
modes.example: In case of overdosage, erythromycin should be<< discontinued>>.

card.writes: It favors words like except, altogether and temporarily, which fit instructions to stop a drug entirely or for a time.
card.plain: It marks spots where the label tells you to stop or pause a particular drug.
